messages:
deploy-bot: Starting progressive rollout v3.4.1 -> region weights: global=100, eu-east=20, eu-west=10, apac=5. Canary window set to 20m. Release ID: rel-3.4.1-20260315

incident-bot: [ALERT] SLO breaches detected: increased 5xx rate in eu-east. Triggering paging for on-call.

Sam O.: On it. Waking up — give me a minute to pull metrics.

Maria H.: I'm seeing a spike in 502/504 from the runtime pool serving eu-east. Latency spiked ~600ms for short-gen calls.

Aditi S.: Support already getting customer reports — two high-tier customers in EU seeing errors from embed and chat endpoints. Escalating to P1.

Sam O.: Paging; starting quick triage. Any recent infra changes? Deploy-bot, was there any region override?

deploy-bot: rel-3.4.1 included a traffic-split update. Config change pushed at 03:12 UTC: set eu-east weight=20. No schema changes.

Leo C.: I pulled LB metrics — there was a sudden jump in requests into eu-east at ~03:15. Looks like the traffic-split controller accidentally applied new weight to eu-east and eu-west, but eu-east was not yet warm (some hosts still initializing kv caches).

Jen K.: Confirmed customers impacted: acct-redwood-enterprise-1 and acct-quant-saas show request failures and retries. Need mitigation now. What's the rollback plan?

Maria H.: Two mitigations: 1) reduce eu-east weight to 0 (kill the surge), 2) if that fails, rollback the rollout entirely. Prefer weight adjust first to avoid full rollback and global churn.

Sam O.: Agreed. Applying emergency weight adjust to route controller. Running command now:

Sam O.: ```
# reduce eu-east to 0 and shift to fallback region
curl -XPOST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CTRL_TOKEN' 
  https://control.redwood.internal/route-split 
  -d '{"route":"inference","overrides":{"eu-east":0}}'
```

incident-bot: Action taken: route-split update submitted by Sam O. (request id r-9b3f).

Aditi S.: Support: letting affected customers know we're actively mitigating and will follow up with ETA. Posting status note in customer dashboard.

Maria H.: Monitoring — 5xx count dropping in eu-east after the change, latencies also trending down. Still seeing a small tail as host kv caches drain.

Sam O.: Good. Next: mark release canary as failed and abort further region expansions. I'm applying canary kill-switch in the rollout controller. Command:

Sam O.: ```
# abort canary and freeze traffic changes
POST /api/releases/rel-3.4.1/abort
{ "reason": "eu-east spike; aborting canary and freezing rollout" }
```

deploy-bot: Canary aborted for rel-3.4.1. All automated rollouts paused.

Leo C.: One notable finding — `cacheWarmStrategy=v2` gate didn't flip for a subset of inference nodes in eu-east due to an inconsistent feature-flag evaluation; that mismatch caused unprimed KV caches to receive full traffic suddenly. We'll open a follow-up.

Jen K.: Customer impact summary for pager: about 2% of global traffic, but affects high-SLA EU customers. Affected window ~03:15–03:22 UTC. We've pushed status updates to customers.

Sam O.: On-call handoff: I'm staying on until stabilization, but I'll do a formal handoff in 30m to Maria if things look green. Maria, please prepare remediation checklist and postmortem outline.

Maria H.: Will do. Immediate action items: 1) confirm eu-east hosts recovered and caches warmed, 2) audit traffic-split controller logs for why weight applied early, 3) reproduce FF evaluation mismatch in staging, 4) write runbook step to block weight changes until warm checks pass.

Aditi S.: Support follow-up: created incident case INC-5421 for each customer and scheduled one-on-one outreach for the two affected enterprise accounts.

Sam O.: Last note before handoff — run quick verification script to ensure no more 5xx across regions: `scripts/verify-global-health.sh --since 03:00 --regions eu-east,eu-west,apac`. Results all green at 03:30. Handing to Maria for postmortem and follow-ups. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident closed to on-call after handoff to SRE. Postmortem required per incident policy (impact > 1% & enterprise customers).
